newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh marchers damage vehicles on strike eve.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh marchers damage vehicles on strike eve.

text.p: Activists preparing for a countrywide general strike called by the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) for Sunday marched with flaming torches and attacked vehicles in the capital Dhaka and other cities.
Police made no attempt to stop one such attack near Dhaka's Ramna police station, not far from the office of BNP chief Begum Khaleda Zia, witnesses said.
"We will smash everything...and enforce the strike," one attacker yelled.
The BNP called the strike for Sunday, a working day in mainly Moslem Bangladesh, in its first major attempt to destabilise the eight-month-old government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
In the southern port city of Chittagong, hundreds of BNP activists staged a torch march and exploded several home-made bombs, witnesses said. No casualties were reported.
BNP activists also demonstrated in Khulna and other cities, asking residents to help make the strike a success.
Police said they had been asked by authorities not to deal with the strikers too harshly.
Hasina took office last June, defeating the BNP in a general election billed as free and fair by local and international monitors.
